stance.probabilities_note: Market-implied Fed path, read from the curve instead of the licensed CME futures feed: the gap between the 1-year Treasury and the current target midpoint. Positive = easing priced, negative = tightening priced. A real signal, not an option-implied probability.
stance.caveat: The Fed does not set mortgage rates. It moves the front end; mortgage rates follow the 10Y and the MBS spread.

cells.name: Easing Priced In, 1Y
cells.notes: Basis points of cuts the 1-year Treasury is pricing versus the current fed funds target midpoint. Positive = the market expects easing, negative = hikes. A real read on Fed expectations straight from the curve, in place of the licensed CME FedWatch probability.

transmission_note: The Fed does not set mortgage rates. It sets the overnight rate. That moves expectations for growth and inflation, which move Treasury yields, which move MBS yields, which move mortgage rates. The chain can break at any link. In September through December 2024 the Fed cut 100 bp and the 30-year mortgage rate rose roughly 100 bp, because the 10-year sold off.
